mainTopic: End of the משנה on private במות, and the argument over 'חוץ מגתה' for the פרה אדומה and whether the מבול reached ארץ ישראל
overview: This amud finishes the משנה's list of Temple rules that do not apply on a private במה, such as needing a כהן or priestly clothes. It then names the rules that apply everywhere: פיגול, נותר and טומאה. The גמרא asks what 'חוץ מגתה' means for the פרה אדומה. ריש לקיש says it means outside the spot checked for graves. רבי יוחנן objects that all of ארץ ישראל counts as checked, so he explains it as slaughtering the פרה inside the walls of ירושלים. The גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן did not use the case of slaughtering outside the wall but not facing the entrance. It answers that he chose the more surprising case. It then shows that their argument depends on whether the מבול reached ארץ ישראל, which each side reads from the same פסוק in יחזקאל. Each side challenges the other, from the courtyards built for the פרה and from רבי יהושע's protest, and a new question begins that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: No placing blood all around, no waving, no bringing near on a private במה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה finishes its list of altar actions that a private במה does not need. רבי יהודה adds that no מנחה is brought on a במה at all.
steps.simpleTranslation: On a private במה there is no placing of blood all around the altar, no waving, and no bringing the מנחה to the altar. רבי יהודה says: no מנחה is brought on a במה at all.
steps.whatsHappening: We are joining the משנה in the middle of a list of Temple rules that do not apply on a private במה. Here it names the last three, and רבי יהודה adds his own view.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא only says that the special steps of a מנחה (תנופה and הגשה) are skipped on a במה, so he holds a מנחה can still be brought there. רבי יהודה goes further and says a מנחה cannot be brought on a במה at all.

keyTerms.meaning: Putting the blood on all sides of the altar
Waving an offering back and forth
Bringing the מנחה to the corner of the altar
An altar outside the Temple, used when private altars were allowed
A flour offering

phrases.english: And placement of blood all around,
phrases.notes: This picks up the משנה's list of things there is 'no' of on a private במה.

phrases.english: and waving, and bringing near.
Rabbi Yehuda says:
There is no meal offering on a private altar.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: אֵין מִנְחָה בְּבָמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list from the earlier part of the daf
steps.mimraCoreRuling: On a private במה there is no מתן סביב, תנופה or הגשה. רבי יהודה holds no מנחה is brought there at all.

steps.title: No כהן, priestly clothes, vessels or washing needed on a private במה
steps.stepSummary: The משנה lists more Temple requirements that do not apply on a private במה: a כהן, בגדי שרת, כלי שרת, ריח ניחוח, the red line for the blood, and washing hands and feet.
steps.simpleTranslation: Also, on a private במה you do not need a כהן, priestly clothes, Temple vessels, a pleasing smell, the dividing line for the blood, or washing of hands and feet.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה goes back to its main list and adds more Temple rules that a private במה does not need.
steps.deeperAnalysis: These are all rules about who does the service and how the Temple service is carried out. On a private במה anyone may bring the offering, without the full Temple routine.

keyTerms.meaning: The service has to be done by a כהן
The special clothes of the כהנים
The holy Temple vessels
The red line dividing the upper and lower halves of the altar
The כהן washing his hands and feet before the service

steps.confusionAlert: These words are not part of רבי יהודה's statement. The משנה is going back to its own list of things that are not needed on a private במה.

phrases.english: And priesthood, and service vestments,
and service vessels, and a pleasing aroma,
and a partition for the blood,
and washing of hands and feet.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִיהוּן, וּבִגְדֵי שָׁרֵת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes on with the list of things not needed on a private במה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A כהן, בגדי שרת, כלי שרת, ריח ניחוח, the red line and washing are not needed on a private במה.

steps.title: פיגול, נותר and טומאה apply on both kinds of altar
steps.stepSummary: The משנה ends by saying which rules are the same on a private במה and the big altar: the time rule (פיגול), leftovers (נותר), and טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the rules of time (פיגול), leftovers (נותר), and impurity are the same on both kinds of altar.
steps.whatsHappening: After listing the differences, the משנה names the rules that stay exactly the same on both altars.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rules about how the service is done are relaxed on a private במה. But the rules that guard the holiness of the offering itself still apply: a wrong-time intention, eating after the time limit, and eating while טמא.

keyTerms.meaning: Planning to eat or offer after the allowed time, which makes the offering פיגול
Meat left over past the time it may be eaten
Ritually impure, here the ban on eating holy meat while impure
Equal in this one and in that one

steps.whatToRemember: A private במה skips many Temple procedures, but פיגול, נותר and טומאה apply there just as on the big altar.

phrases.english: But the time rule,
phrases.notes: The wrong-time intention that makes an offering פיגול.

phrases.english: the leftover, and the impure —
are equal in this and in that.
phrases.notes: 'This and that' means the private במה and the big altar.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל הַזְּמַן, הַנּוֹתָר וְהַטָּמֵא – שָׁוִין בָּזֶה וּבָזֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ends the list of differences by naming what is the same
steps.mimraCoreRuling: פיגול, נותר and טומאה apply equally on a private במה and the big altar.

steps.title: What does 'outside its pit' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens by asking about an earlier line of the משנה: what does 'חוץ מגתה' mean for the פרה אדומה?
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: What does 'outside its pit' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and goes back to an earlier line of the משנה, asking what 'חוץ מגתה' means. This sets up the answers that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier the משנה said that someone who burns the פרה אדומה 'חוץ מגתה' is not liable for offering outside the Temple. The word 'גת' (literally a pit) is unclear, so the גמרא asks what place it means.

keyTerms.meaning: The Talmud's discussion of the משנה
What?
Outside its pit, meaning outside the proper place for the פרה אדומה

phrases.english: GEMARA
What is 'outside its pit'?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי חוּץ מִגִּתָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts the גמרא and goes back to an earlier line of the משנה
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which place is meant by 'גתה' in the case of the פרה אדומה

steps.title: ריש לקיש: outside the place checked for graves
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש explains 'חוץ מגתה' as outside the spot that was checked to make sure it has no graves.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: it means outside the place that was checked for it.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש answers the question. 'Its pit' means the special spot that was checked for טומאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פרה אדומה must be done in a very pure way. So ריש לקיש says it has a specific spot that was checked to make sure no grave is there. Burning it anywhere else is 'outside its pit.'

keyTerms.meaning: A place that was checked, here for graves and טומאה

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said:
Outside the place that was inspected for it.
phrases.notes: 'Inspected' means checked to make sure no grave is hidden there, so the spot is pure.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ: חוּץ מִמָּקוֹם הַבָּדוּק לָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 4
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'חוץ מגתה' means outside the place checked for טומאה

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: all of ארץ ישראל is already checked
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן challenges ריש לקיש: all of ארץ ישראל counts as checked, so there is no special checked spot that could be meant.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said to him: But isn't all of ארץ ישראל already checked?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן attacks ריש לקיש's answer. If all of ארץ ישראל is considered checked, then 'outside the checked place' cannot be the meaning.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש's answer only works if there is a place that is not checked. רבי יוחנן says the whole land counts as checked, so there would be no 'outside' spot at all.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it so that...? (a challenge)
Checked, presumed to be pure

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said to him:
But is not all of Eretz Yisrael
inspected!

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: וַהֲלֹא כׇּל אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּדוּקָה הִיא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges ריש לקיש's answer
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: All of ארץ ישראל counts as checked, so there is no unchecked place that 'outside' could refer to

steps.title: רבי יוחנן: the פרה was slaughtered inside the walls of ירושלים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן gives his own explanation: 'חוץ מגתה' is a case where the פרה אדומה was slaughtered inside the walls of ירושלים instead of outside.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבי יוחנן said: for example, where he slaughtered it inside the wall of ירושלים.
steps.whatsHappening: Having rejected ריש לקיש's answer, רבי יוחנן gives a new explanation. 'Outside its pit' means it was slaughtered inside ירושלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פרה אדומה must be done outside the city. So 'outside its proper place' is a case where it was wrongly done inside the walls. Even so, the person is not liable for offering outside the Temple, because the פרה is not an offering of the Temple courtyard.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather; drops the earlier answer and gives a new one
For example, such as
The wall of ירושלים

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן says 'חוץ מגתה' means the פרה אדומה was slaughtered inside ירושלים instead of in its proper place outside the walls.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
For example, where he slaughtered it
inside the wall of Jerusalem.
phrases.notes: The פרה is supposed to be done outside the camp (במדבר 19:3), so inside the walls is the wrong place.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כְּגוֹן שֶׁשְּׁחָטָהּ לִפְנִים מִן חוֹמַת יְרוּשָׁלַיִם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces ריש לקיש's rejected answer with a new explanation
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'חוץ מגתה' means the פרה was slaughtered inside the walls of ירושלים

steps.title: Why not explain it as slaughtering outside the wall but not facing the entrance?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבי יוחנן didn't explain 'חוץ מגתה' as slaughtering the פרה אדומה outside the wall but not facing the entrance.
steps.simpleTranslation: But let him explain it as a case where he slaughtered it outside the wall, but not facing the entrance!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יוחנן's explanation from Step 7. It suggests a different case he could have used for 'חוץ מגתה'.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן said 'חוץ מגתה' means slaughtering inside ירושלים. The גמרא points out another way to get it wrong: going outside the wall as required, but not standing opposite the entrance. If that is also פסול, why didn't he choose that case?

keyTerms.meaning: But let him set it up as (explain the case as)
Outside the wall of ירושלים
Facing (opposite) the entrance of the היכל

phrases.english: But let him explain it as a case where he slaughtered it
phrases.notes: 'It' is the משנה's case of 'חוץ מגתה', and 'him' is רבי יוחנן.

phrases.english: outside the wall, but not facing the entrance!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְלוֹקְמַהּ כְּגוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the case רבי יוחנן chose in Step 7
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's explanation that 'חוץ מגתה' means slaughtered inside the walls of ירושלים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Slaughtering outside the wall but not facing the entrance is also פסול for רבי יוחנן, so he could have used that case instead.

steps.title: רב אדא בר אהבה: slaughter must face the entrance
steps.stepSummary: רב אדא בר אהבה learns from a היקש that the slaughter must face the entrance, just like the sprinkling.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רב אדא בר אהבה said: If he slaughtered it not facing the entrance, it is פסול, as it says 'and he shall slaughter… and he shall sprinkle'. Just as its sprinkling is facing the entrance, so too its slaughter must be facing the entrance.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source showing that slaughtering not facing the entrance really is פסול. This supports the challenge in Step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק puts slaughtering and sprinkling next to each other. The sprinkling is clearly done toward the front of the אהל מועד. Because the two are linked, the slaughter must face the entrance too.

keyTerms.meaning: Invalid (the פרה אדומה is disqualified)
Its sprinkling (of the blood)
Its slaughter
Just as… so too… (the form of a comparison)

phrases.english: For Rav Adda bar Ahava said:
If he slaughtered it not facing the entrance, it is invalid,
as it says: 'And he shall slaughter… and he shall sprinkle',
phrases.notes: במדבר 19:3–4. The sprinkling there is toward the front of the אהל מועד.

phrases.english: just as its sprinkling is facing the entrance,
so too its slaughter must be facing the entrance.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּאָמַר רַב אַדָּא בַּר אַהֲבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source behind the premise of the challenge
steps.raayaObject: That slaughtering the פרה אדומה not facing the entrance makes it פסול
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב אדא בר אהבה's היקש linking 'ושחט' with 'והזה'

steps.title: רבי יוחנן himself holds this comparison
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא blocks the reply that רבי יוחנן doesn't accept the היקש. It is recorded that he rules it פסול for exactly this reason, against ריש לקיש.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you will say that he does not make this comparison, it was stated: If he slaughtered it not facing the entrance, רבי יוחנן says it is פסול, because of 'and he shall slaughter… and he shall sprinkle'. ריש לקיש says it is כשר, because of 'outside the camp, and he shall slaughter'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא expects a reply: maybe רבי יוחנן doesn't agree with רב אדא's comparison. It rejects that reply by showing רבי יוחנן clearly does hold it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a recorded מחלוקת on this exact case. רבי יוחנן says פסול using the same היקש. ריש לקיש says כשר, because the פסוק only requires 'outside the camp', so any spot outside works. Since רבי יוחנן holds the rule, the challenge against him is stronger.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you will say (the גמרא expects a reply)
Makes a היקש (compares two things written next to each other)
But it was stated (bringing a recorded teaching of אמוראים)
Valid

phrases.english: And if you will say that he does not make the comparison,
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי יוחנן: maybe he doesn't link slaughtering to sprinkling.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָא אִתְּמַר: שְׁחָטָהּ שֶׁלֹּא כְּנֶגֶד הַפֶּתַח –
phrases.english: but it was stated: If he slaughtered it not facing the entrance,
Rabbi Yochanan says: It is invalid, because of 'and he shall slaughter… and he shall sprinkle'.
Reish Lakish says: It is valid,
because of 'outside the camp, and he shall slaughter'.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵּימָא דְּלָא מַקֵּישׁ, וְהָא אִתְּמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Blocks a possible escape from the challenge by proving רבי יוחנן holds רב אדא's rule
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוחנן himself rules slaughter not facing the entrance פסול
steps.raayaSupportSource: A recorded מחלוקת between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש

steps.title: רבי יוחנן also requires the burning to face the entrance
steps.stepSummary: A second מחלוקת, about burning not facing the entrance, shows רבי יוחנן uses the same comparison for burning too.
steps.simpleTranslation: And it was also stated: If he burned it not facing the entrance, רבי יוחנן says it is פסול and רבי אושעיא says it is כשר. רבי יוחנן says פסול because of 'and he shall burn… and he shall sprinkle'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another recorded מחלוקת. It shows how firmly רבי יוחנן holds the 'facing the entrance' rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן applies the היקש to sprinkling here as well, so the burning also has to face the entrance. This adds weight to the point that, for him, this location rule really matters.

keyTerms.meaning: And it was also stated
He burned it
And he shall burn (from the פסוק)

phrases.aramaic: וְאִיתְּמַר נָמֵי, שְׂרָפָהּ שֶׁלֹּא כְּנֶגֶד הַפֶּתַח –
phrases.english: And it was also stated: If he burned it not facing the entrance,
Rabbi Yochanan says: It is invalid,
and Rabbi Oshaya says: It is valid.
Rabbi Yochanan says invalid, because of 'and he shall burn… and he shall sprinkle'.
phrases.notes: במדבר 19:4–5. The burning is written right after the sprinkling, so they are linked.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִיתְּמַר נָמֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second recorded מחלוקת showing the same view of רבי יוחנן
steps.raayaObject: That רבי יוחנן consistently requires the פרה אדומה service to face the entrance
steps.raayaSupportSource: The מחלוקת of רבי יוחנן and רבי אושעיא about burning

steps.title: רבי אושעיא: burn it where it dies
steps.stepSummary: רבי אושעיא reads 'על פרשה ישרף' as 'where it dies, there it is burned', so the burning has no fixed direction.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי אושעיא says it is כשר, because of 'with its dung it shall be burned'. The place where it departs to death, that is where its burning should be.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains רבי אושעיא's reason for saying the burning is כשר. This ends the background, and the next step answers the challenge against רבי יוחנן from Step 8.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי אושעיא reads 'פרשה' as related to 'פורשת', meaning departing from life. So the פרה is burned wherever it was slaughtered and died, with no need to face the entrance.

keyTerms.meaning: With its dung it shall be burned (במדבר 19:5)
Departs to death (dies)
Its burning

steps.whatToRemember: For רבי יוחנן, the slaughter and burning of the פרה אדומה must both face the entrance, linked to the sprinkling. That is why the גמרא asks why he didn't use 'not facing the entrance' to explain 'חוץ מגתה'.

phrases.english: And Rabbi Oshaya says it is valid,
because of 'with its dung it shall be burned';
phrases.notes: He reads פִּרְשָׁהּ like the word פּוֹרֶשֶׁת, departing, which explains the next line.

phrases.english: the place where it departs to death,
there shall be its burning.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי אוֹשַׁעְיָא אָמַר כְּשֵׁרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the other side's reasoning in the burning מחלוקת
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Burning not facing the entrance is כשר, because the פרה is burned wherever it died.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן taught the bigger 'even' case
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי יוחנן used a 'לא מיבעיא' style. Of course slaughtering outside the wall but not facing the entrance is פסול. He wanted to teach that even inside the wall it is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: They answer: he was speaking in a 'no need to say' style. There is no need to say that outside the wall is invalid, because he moved it farther away. But even inside the wall, where he brought it closer, and you might think it should be valid, he teaches us that it is invalid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question from step 8 about why רבי יוחנן did not explain 'חוץ מגתה' as outside the wall but not facing the entrance.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 9–11 showed that רבי יוחנן agrees the slaughter must face the entrance, so the outside-the-wall case is obviously פסול. The real chiddush is the inside-the-wall case. Someone might think coming closer to the בית המקדש is fine, so רבי יוחנן chose that case to teach that it is still פסול.

keyTerms.meaning: 'No need to say'. A style that skips the obvious case to teach a bigger one.
Outside the wall of ירושלים
Inside the wall
He comes to teach us

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן holds that slaughtering the פרה אדומה not facing the entrance is פסול. He mentioned the inside-the-wall case because it is the surprising one.

phrases.english: They say: he is speaking in a 'no need to say' style;
there is no need to say that outside the wall is invalid,
since he moved it farther away;
phrases.notes: Farther away from the place facing the entrance of the היכל, where it belongs.

phrases.english: but even inside the wall,
where he brought it closer,
and you might say it should be valid,
he teaches us that it is invalid.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרִי: לָא מִיבַּעְיָא קָאָמַר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the קשיא of step 8 now that steps 9–11 have shown רבי יוחנן requires facing the entrance.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Style of teaching (לא מיבעיא). He chose the less obvious case.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Inside the wall might be valid because it is closer to the בית המקדש.
steps.terutzMaskana: Both cases are פסול. רבי יוחנן taught the surprising one.

steps.title: What is the root of the argument about checking the land?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings back רבי יוחנן's words to ריש לקיש, 'Isn't all of ארץ ישראל checked?', and asks what their argument really depends on.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: רבי יוחנן said to him, 'But isn't all of ארץ ישראל checked?' About what do they disagree?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to an earlier argument and asks what the two sides really disagree about. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש required the burning place to be checked for טומאה, and רבי יוחנן said all of ארץ ישראל is already considered checked. The גמרא now wants the reason behind each view.

keyTerms.meaning: Checked, meaning known to be free of hidden graves
About what do they disagree?

phrases.english: The Master said,
Rabbi Yochanan said to him:
phrases.notes: 'Him' is ריש לקיש, from the earlier argument.

phrases.aramaic: וַהֲלֹא כׇּל אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל בְּדוּקָה הִיא.
phrases.english: But isn't all of Eretz Yisrael checked?
About what do they disagree?

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר מָר, אָמַר לוֹ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the facing-the-entrance topic and goes back to the earlier argument about checking the burning place.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The underlying reason for the מחלוקת between רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש.

steps.title: Did the מבול reach ארץ ישראל?
steps.stepSummary: The argument depends on whether the מבול came down on ארץ ישראל. ריש לקיש says it did, and רבי יוחנן says it did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: One master holds the flood came down on ארץ ישראל, and the other master holds it did not.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its question: the two sides disagree about whether the מבול reached ארץ ישראל.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the מבול came, people died everywhere in the land, so a grave could be hiding anywhere and the spot must be checked (ריש לקיש). If it never came, there is no such worry, and the land counts as checked (רבי יוחנן).

keyTerms.meaning: The flood in the days of נח
One master holds

steps.confusionAlert: Each 'מר' refers to a different person. The first is ריש לקיש, who says the מבול came. The second is רבי יוחנן, who says it did not.

phrases.aramaic: מָר סָבַר: יָרַד מַבּוּל לְאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל,
phrases.english: One master holds: the flood came down on Eretz Yisrael,
and the other master holds: it did not come down.

steps.triggerLanguage: מָר סָבַר: יָרַד מַבּוּל לְאֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the שאלה of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מחלוקת depends on whether the מבול fell on ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: Both sides learn from one verse
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן בר יצחק says that רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש both learned their views from the same פסוק in יחזקאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן בר יצחק said: both of them learned from one verse: 'Son of man, say to her: You are a land that is not cleansed, not rained upon in the day of anger.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן בר יצחק brings the פסוק both sides use. This sets up the next step, which shows how each one reads it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the מחלוקת about the מבול is linked to a source. The same words support both views, so the difference must come from how the פסוק is read.

keyTerms.meaning: They learned from one and the same פסוק
Not cleansed or purified
Day of anger, here the time of the מבול

phrases.english: Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak said,
and both of them learned from one verse:
'Son of man, say to her:
You are a land that is not cleansed,
not rained upon in the day of anger.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב נַחְמָן בַּר יִצְחָק, וּשְׁנֵיהֶם מִקְרָא אֶחָד דָּרְשׁוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source behind the two positions from step 15.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both רבי יוחנן and ריש לקיש base their views on יחזקאל 22:24.

steps.title: A question or a plain statement?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן reads the פסוק as a surprised question: 'Are you not pure? Did the flood's rains fall on you?' So the land is pure. ריש לקיש reads it plainly: 'You are not pure. Didn't rains fall on you?' So the flood did reach it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן holds the פסוק is asking in amazement: 'ארץ ישראל, are you not pure?! Did rains fall on you on the day of anger?!' ריש לקיש holds it means what it plainly says: 'You are a land that is not pure. Didn't rains fall on you on the day of anger?!'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how each side reads the same פסוק to reach opposite views about the מבול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For רבי יוחנן, 'לא מטהרה' is a question meaning 'of course you are pure', because no flood rain fell there. For ריש לקיש, 'לא מטהרה' is a plain statement that the land is impure, because the flood's rains did fall there. Whether the flood came decides if graves could be hidden anywhere.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק is asking in amazement, a question that expects the opposite answer
According to its simple meaning
'Did... at all?' A word that opens a doubtful question

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוחנן: the מבול never reached ארץ ישראל, so the whole land counts as checked. ריש לקיש: the מבול did reach it, so the place for burning the פרה אדומה must be checked. Both read יחזקאל 22:24, one as a question and one as a statement.
steps.confusionAlert: Both readings use the very same words. The only difference is the tone: רבי יוחנן reads 'not cleansed' as a surprised question, and ריש לקיש reads it as a plain statement.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan holds,
the verse is asking in amazement:

phrases.aramaic: אֶרֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵל, מִי לָא מְטוֹהָרָה אַתְּ?!
phrases.english: Eretz Yisrael, are you not pure?!

phrases.aramaic: כְּלוּם יָרְדוּ עָלַיִךְ גְּשָׁמִים בְּיוֹם זָעַם?!
phrases.english: Did rains fall on you on the day of anger?!
phrases.notes: The 'day of anger' here means the time of the מבול.

phrases.english: And Reish Lakish holds: it means what it plainly says:
You are a land that is not pure;

phrases.aramaic: מִי לֹא יָרְדוּ עָלַיִךְ גְּשָׁמִים בְּיוֹם זָעַם?!
phrases.english: didn't rains fall on you on the day of anger?!

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן סָבַר, אַתְמוֹהֵי מַתְמַהּ קְרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains how each side reads the פסוק quoted in step 16.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יוחנן reads the פסוק as a rhetorical question, so the מבול did not fall on ארץ ישראל. ריש לקיש reads it plainly, so the מבול did fall there.

steps.title: ריש לקיש challenges from the פרה אדומה courtyards
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש challenges רבי יוחנן from a משנה. In ירושלים, special courtyards were built over a hollow space because of hidden graves deep underground. Children were raised there in purity to help with the פרה אדומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש challenged רבי יוחנן: There were courtyards in ירושלים built on rock, with a hollow space under them, in case there was a hidden grave deep below. They brought pregnant women there to give birth and raise their children for the פרה אדומה. They brought oxen with doors on their backs. The children sat on the doors holding stone cups. They filled the cups and sat back in their places.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש brings a משנה to show that people did worry about hidden graves, even in ירושלים. This seems to go against רבי יוחנן, who said ארץ ישראל is checked and has no hidden bodies.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If there were no hidden bodies in ארץ ישראל, why build a hollow space under the courtyards and seat the children on doors? These steps show a real worry about unknown graves deep in the ground. That fits ריש לקיש, who holds the מבול left dead bodies in ארץ ישראל too.

keyTerms.meaning: A grave hidden deep underground that nobody knows about
The red heifer, whose ashes purify people from the impurity of a dead body
Stone cups, which cannot become טמא

phrases.english: Reish Lakish raised an objection to Rabbi Yochanan:
There were courtyards in Jerusalem
built on rock,
and beneath them was a hollow space
because of a grave in the depths,
and they would bring pregnant women, and they would give birth there,
and raise their children there for the red heifer.
And they would bring oxen,
and on their backs were doors,
and the children would sit on them,
phrases.notes: The doors act as a barrier between the children and any grave in the ground underneath.

phrases.english: with cups of stone in their hands,
and they filled them and sat back in their places.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רֵישׁ לָקִישׁ לְרַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After both sides' readings of the פסוק were explained, ריש לקיש brings a משנה to attack רבי יוחנן's view.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יוחנן's claim that ארץ ישראל is checked and has no hidden graves from the מבול.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה shows serious steps taken against hidden graves deep under ירושלים, which only makes sense if such graves might exist.

steps.title: An extra stringency just for the פרה אדומה
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא בריה דרב יהושע answers for רבי יוחנן: those courtyards were an extra stringency made only for the פרה אדומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא, the son of רב יהושע, said: They made an extra stringency for the פרה אדומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends רבי יוחנן. The courtyards do not prove there are hidden graves. They were an extra level of care just for the פרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By the basic law there is no real worry about hidden graves in ארץ ישראל, just as רבי יוחנן said. For the פרה אדומה, חז"ל demanded extra purity, so they guarded even against an unlikely risk. So the משנה shows a special stringency, not a general worry.

keyTerms.meaning: An extra stringency, a higher standard beyond the basic law

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a common move in the גמרא: a strict practice in a special area like פרה אדומה does not prove what the basic law is everywhere.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב הוּנָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב יְהוֹשֻׁעַ:
phrases.english: Rav Huna, son of Rav Yehoshua, said:
They made an extra stringency for the red heifer.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַעֲלָה עָשׂוּ בַּפָּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers ריש לקיש's challenge in step 18 on behalf of רבי יוחנן.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the source: the practice was a special stringency, not basic law.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The courtyards prove that hidden graves are a real worry in ירושלים.
steps.terutzMaskana: The courtyards were only an extra stringency for the פרה, so רבי יוחנן's view still stands.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן challenges from רבי יהושע's protest
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן challenges ריש לקיש from a story. Bones were found in a chamber of the בית המקדש, and the חכמים wanted to declare ירושלים impure. רבי יהושע protested: 'Where are the dead of the flood? Where are the dead of נבוכדנצר?'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן challenged ריש לקיש: Once bones were found in the Chamber of the Woodshed, and they wanted to declare ירושלים impure. רבי יהושע stood up and said: Isn't it a shame and disgrace for us to declare our fathers' city impure? Where are the dead of the flood? Where are the dead of נבוכדנצר?
steps.whatsHappening: Now רבי יוחנן fights back with a story where רבי יהושע refused to worry about hidden bodies in ירושלים. He speaks as if there are no dead of the מבול there, which seems to go against ריש לקיש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש holds the מבול reached ארץ ישראל, so dead bodies could be buried anywhere. But רבי יהושע asks 'Where are the dead of the flood?', meaning we do not find or worry about them in ירושלים. That fits רבי יוחנן, who says the מבול never came there.

keyTerms.meaning: The Chamber of the Woodshed, a room in the בית המקדש where wood was kept
To make a rule declaring a place impure
Shame and disgrace
The people who died in the flood

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan raised an objection to Reish Lakish:
Once they found bones
in the Chamber of the Woodshed,
and they wanted to decree impurity on Jerusalem.

phrases.aramaic: עָמַד רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ עַל רַגְלָיו וְאָמַר:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua stood on his feet and said:
Is it not a shame and disgrace for us
to decree impurity on the city of our fathers?!
Where are the dead of the flood?
Where are the dead of Nebuchadnezzar?
phrases.notes: נבוכדנצר killed many people when he conquered ירושלים, yet we don't treat the city as full of hidden graves.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֵיתִיבֵיהּ רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן לְרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After רבי יוחנן's view was defended in step 19, the challenges switch direction: now רבי יוחנן attacks ריש לקיש.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that the מבול came down on ארץ ישראל, so hidden dead may be there.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהושע speaks as if there are no dead of the flood in ירושלים to worry about, which fits רבי יוחנן's view that the מבול did not reach ארץ ישראל.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן draws his proof from רבי יהושע's words
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן argues that רבי יהושע's question 'Where are the dead of the flood?' means there were no flood-dead in ירושלים, so the flood never reached ארץ ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since רבי יהושע said this, doesn't it mean that there were no such dead there?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן finishes the challenge from step 20 by spelling out what he learns from רבי יהושע's words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע asked, 'Where are the dead of the flood?' רבי יוחנן reads this as 'there are none here.' If no one died there in the flood, then the flood never came to ארץ ישראל, which goes against ריש לקיש.

keyTerms.meaning: From the fact that he says
Doesn't this mean to say...?
They did not exist / there were none

phrases.english: From the fact that he said this,
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי יהושע, who asked, 'Where are the dead of the flood?' in step 20.

phrases.english: is it not to say that there were none?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִדְּקָאָמַר הָכִי, לָאו לְמֵימְרָא דְּלָא הֲווֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the challenge begun in step 20 by drawing the inference from רבי יהושע's words.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's view that the flood reached ארץ ישראל
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: 'Where are the flood-dead?' implies there were none in ירושלים, so the flood never came there.

steps.title: ריש לקיש answers: the dead existed but were cleared away
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש points out that the same sentence mentions the dead of נבוכדנצר, who certainly existed. So רבי יהושע meant that the bodies were there but were removed. The same applies to the flood-dead.
steps.simpleTranslation: And by your logic, the people killed by נבוכדנצר also never existed?! Rather, they existed and were cleared away. Here too, the flood-dead existed and were cleared away.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש turns רבי יוחנן's reading against him, using the second half of רבי יהושע's own sentence.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If 'Where are they?' meant 'they never existed,' it would have to mean that about נבוכדנצר's victims too, and that is plainly false. So 'Where are they?' must mean 'they were removed long ago.' This keeps ריש לקיש's view that the flood did reach ארץ ישראל.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your reasoning
The people killed by נבוכדנצר
They cleared them away (removed the bodies)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהושע's 'Where are they?' does not prove that the dead never existed. Both the flood-dead and נבוכדנצר's victims were there and were later removed.

phrases.english: And according to your reasoning,

phrases.aramaic: הֲרוּגֵי נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר הָכִי נָמֵי דְּלָא הֲווֹ?!
phrases.english: those killed by Nebuchadnezzar, so too were there none?!
Rather, there were, and they removed them;
here too, there were, and they removed them.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּלְטַעְמָיךְ, הֲרוּגֵי נְבוּכַדְנֶצַּר הָכִי נָמֵי דְּלָא הֲווֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the inference drawn in step 21.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי יוחנן's reading of רבי יהושע's words as proof that there were no flood-dead.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: That reading would also force the absurd claim that נבוכדנצר's victims never existed.

steps.title: Opening a new question: if the bodies were removed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a new question: if the bodies were cleared away, why should there be any worry about hidden graves?
steps.simpleTranslation: And if they were cleared away...
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is starting a new question, and the rest of it continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ריש לקיש just said the bodies were removed. That raises a problem for his own view: if they are gone, why must the place for burning the פרה אדומה be checked for graves (step 5)? The full question comes next.

keyTerms.meaning: And if they were cleared away

steps.confusionAlert: The question is not finished here. Don't look for the answer yet; the next lines complete the question.

phrases.english: And if they were removed,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי אִפַּנּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Accepts step 22's claim that the bodies were removed and uses it to question ריש לקיש's need for a checked place.
steps.kashyaTarget: ריש לקיש's requirement that the place for the פרה אדומה be checked for hidden graves, once he admits the bodies were removed
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the bodies were removed, ריש לקיש's demand that the פרה's place be checked for hidden graves seems unnecessary (the question is completed on the next amud).
